newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU revises wish-list for Japanese deregulation.
newsitem.headline: EU revises wish-list for Japanese deregulation.

text.p: The European Union has revised its list of demands made to the Japanese government for inclusion in Tokyo's ongoing deregulation programme, adding a request for various administrative reforms to a long list.

"Some issues are included in the list for the first time -- such as administrative reform -- and some, like measures related to natural mineral waters, have been removed due to significant progress made already," the European Commission said in a statement on Tuesday.

The 131-page document, released to reporters, covers a wide band of commercial activities targeted by the EU for deregulation, ranging from construction, farm trade and financial services to vehicle manufacture, transport, food and cosmetics.

"Progress has been made in the Japanese deregulation programme, in particular in areas such as telecommunications, financial services, with the exception of insurance, cars and foodstuffs," European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said.
"We have a lot more work to do with Japan in the coming weeks, but I am optimistic that we can make progress," he added.
The issue of administrative reform concerns transparency of laws affecting traders and their predictability.
